ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is quadrilateral P Q R S, with vertex P at the upper left, Q at the upper right, R at the lower right, and S at the lower left. The diagonal QS from S to Q is drawn in the figure, dividing the quadrilateral into two triangles PQS and QRS. Angle P is between sides PQ and PS, and angle R is between sides QR and RS. Reasoning: Given PQ=721, PS=756, QR=547, RS=593, and ∠P=58°. First use the law of cosines in triangle PQS to find the common diagonal QS: QS^2 = PQ^2 + PS^2 - 2(PQ)(PS)cos P = 721^2 + 756^2 - 2(721)(756)cos58° ≈ 513684.45. Therefore QS ≈ 716.72. Then in triangle QRS, the side opposite angle R is QS, so: QS^2 = QR^2 + RS^2 - 2(QR)(RS)cos R. Solving gives: cos R = (QR^2 + RS^2 - QS^2)/(2(QR)(RS)) = (547^2 + 593^2 - 513684.45)/(2·547·593) ≈ 0.21144. So R ≈ arccos(0.21144) ≈ 77.8°.
